diffs.diff: distance_cm (echo pulse width in microseconds): datasheet reading gives 0.01715 per count, the part's model has none
diffs.evidence: The model does carry this conversion, in a form the gate does not extract (ultrasonic sim.echo.usPerCm, not sim.measure): part.json sim.echo.usPerCm = 58.3 us/cm, i.e. 1/58.3 = 0.01715 cm per us, and the driver computes distance_cm = t * 0.0343 / 2 = t * 0.01715 -- identical to the second reading's 0.01715. Adafruit's own HC-SR04/RCWL-1601 library (used for product 4007) states 'sound travels through dry air at 343.2 meters per second (at 20 C)' and converts with '# 1/1000000 s/us * 340 m/s * 100 cm/m * 2 = 0.017 / return pulselen * 0.017' (0.017 vs 0.01715 is only the 340 vs 343 m/s speed-of-sound choice, <1%). Echo high time is the round trip, so cm = us x 0.0343 / 2.
